statement: Inspect available project memory, exact artifacts, lineage, current state, scars, rejected/deferred branches, and frontier before inventing a clean slate.
title: Recover continuity before widening

statement: Use remembered state to find evidence and preserve intent; reverify current facts when the decision depends on them.
title: Memory is continuity, not proof

statement: Import mechanisms, constraints, scars, counterexamples, and experiment designs; donor identity or prestige does not transfer authority.
title: Strip donors for parts

statement: Research branches, donors, prototypes, and candidate mechanisms do not self-promote into canonical or product authority.
title: Separate exploration from promotion

statement: Each pass must answer the discriminator exposed by the prior result; stop at the declared boundary and perform breadth checks.
title: Run bounded discriminator-led campaigns

statement: Test the strongest claim and plausible rivals. Preserve useful failures as scars after repair.
title: Use challenge cases, counterexamples, removals, and altered variants

statement: Use a compact current operational surface plus append-preferred history when durable continuity machinery exists.
title: Keep live state separate from forensic chronology

statement: Checkpoint intent, authority, lineage, evidence, unknowns, scars, and exact next action when work materially changes state.
title: Significant work must survive a fresh instance

statement: A process tool can work correctly and still be unnecessary. Measure whether it improves the research job it exists to serve.
title: Process instruments must earn existence and residency

statement: Do not ship campaign cadence, reviewer choreography, role labels, or other in-house process rules as engineering-product requirements unless the product itself requires them.
title: Internal research governance is not product content

statement: Keep model, prompt/context, tools, persistent state, harness, environment, validators, and operator effects separable when attribution matters.
title: AI-assisted work is a system, not a single model

statement: Role/context changes can improve search but do not acquire independent evidence authority by naming.
title: Same-model self-critique is search, not an independent vote

statement: Models are useful for search, synthesis, code production, translation, and test generation; promotion-bearing claims still need evidence suited to the consequence.
title: Use current AI capability aggressively but verify externally where consequence matters

statement: When a process guard exists because of a specific substrate behavior, preserve the historical failure and retest current enforcement after meaningful substrate change.
title: Requalify era-conditioned process burden instead of fossilizing it

statement: Plans may bound the search, but the result of Pass N earns Pass N+1.
title: Do not prewrite the path through an experiment

statement: Spend vocabulary budget on engineering distinctions, not ornamental phrasing.
title: Use plain language without simplifying mechanisms
